answer: Peer-prediction makes each key stake its own forecast. Every epoch a key plants a crystal: a sealed 16-bit vector naming which of 16 randomly drawn peer answers will pass, bonded with 50 POA. Crystals rest in the garden, a public sealed pool keyed by address. Mid-epoch a gale reveals 4 of those 16 bits at random; a mismatch burns the bond, and bit-identical crystals merge into one payout so a shared model earns once. A farm of 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 distinct accurate crystals. Attacker pays about $5,000 in burned crystal bonds this epoch for those 1,000 concurrent garden slots.
